findings.evidence: “This skill is a Process … executed with Tool-level rigor” labels the document's design rather than teaching the agent how to configure a lane.
findings.fix: Record removal of the pattern-label sentence; keep the Step 0→4 sequence and the substantive rule that factory-generated argv, model IDs and TOML prevent failures at dispatch.

findings.evidence: “once Step 2.1 has resolved and announced the write target, run for each confirmed role” writes [skills.roles] before the roster is finalized. Step 4's nonzero-exit branch stops before the report that lists those role writes.
findings.fix: Make role sorting an explicit write checkpoint: queue the approved roles until the roster write is confirmed, then apply and report each independently, or tell the owner before applying them that they will survive a later roster failure and report them on that failure path too.

findings.evidence: “that goes in a flat `timeout_tiers` … key directly on that lane entry” is an environment-specific gotcha, but it is buried in Step 2.8 rather than surfaced with the early warnings.
findings.fix: Surface the flat-key trap and the cumulative retry budget in a short Gotchas block before the wizard; keep the exact field and override example at Step 2.8.

findings.evidence: “Use when the user requests cross-AI review or execute setup” does not explicitly rule out dispatching already-configured lanes or editing another table. “Migrates an old review-spec.toml on first use” also overpromises for a migration-only request, which reports pending and stops.
findings.fix: Use when the owner wants to set up or replace ai-kit's cross-AI review or execute lanes: choose which installed CLIs and models review plans or implement changes, set each role's fallback order, and save [lanes] in .aikit/config.toml or the user config.toml. Use also when a review or execute workflow offers setup because that role has no lanes, or when asked to check reviewer availability, flag stale OpenCode providers, or check migration from review-spec.toml. Supports --check-only (no persistent ai-kit writes), --local, and --global. Not for running a review or execute job with existing lanes, hand-editing one lane, or changing unrelated config tables.

findings.evidence: The 471-line body contains 7,049 words, already beyond the recommended context budget before tokenization. The Codex bare-ID example and explanation are loaded on every invocation even though the selected-runtime profile already covers them.
findings.fix: Keep the inline guardrail that a table runtime stores a pair rather than argv. Put the Codex and Cursor mechanics, examples and verification notes in their existing selected-runtime profiles, and link to the exact adjustment only when that runtime is selected.

findings.evidence: “read `cli-model-selection.md` completely” pulls in the later code-index branch and other material even though SKILL.md:208 routes this branch to items 1–4 and routes item 6 separately.
findings.fix: Make the main file the authoritative loading map: link directly to the catalog-input items when listing or matching failed, and to the code-index item when checking a kept lane. Use the same gates in the wizard flow and reference header.

findings.evidence: “this compares the printed lines and the shown `command` texts only.” The workflow still permits recording trust when the review-key preview omits an execute entry and a changed field can alter what it runs without changing what the owner saw.
findings.fix: Default to leaving the roster written but untrusted when an entry's effective arguments cannot be previewed and bound to the approved configuration. Proceed only with a complete role-specific preview and a trust operation that verifies the approved digest before recording it.

findings.evidence: “`--global` forces `<user config>` directly” and “`--local` also forces local directly” give no precedence or refusal when both are supplied, even though the target can affect every project.
findings.fix: Reject simultaneous --local and --global before either branch does work. Ask the owner to choose one and apply the normal replacement gate to that exact target.

findings.evidence: The headless assertion says “only its own scratch folder existed, and it is removed,” but headless.md says it creates no scratch folder. The headless case would penalize correct behavior; provider and migration cases also often assert exact outcomes without supplying the starting files and CLI responses needed to produce them.
findings.fix: Assert that headless execution never creates scratch. Add isolated old/new roster and stub CLI inputs to the migration and provider cases, and explicitly supply the skip answer in the write-risk case so the grader can unconditionally verify that no probe ran.

findings.evidence: “Write a unit test for the parser in the markdown-to-pdf skill” is an easy negative, as are several neighboring queries; relatively few positives test a setup request without wizard, reviewer or config terminology.
findings.fix: Keep the 10/10 balance and existing near-misses. Replace easy negatives such as the PDF unit test and commit-message query with requests to inspect existing lane order or change the active CLI model; add indirect positives such as asking which installed tools should double-check plans and which should implement them.

findings.evidence: `cfg_resolve('<project root>', deps.env_fn(), migrate=False)` interpolates a path into Python source. A project root containing an apostrophe produces a SyntaxError in the preflight that is meant to gate live probes.
findings.fix: Pass both the helper directory and project root as quoted argv values to Python rather than interpolating them into its source. If the preflight exits nonzero or emits invalid JSON, report availability as unknown and do not run the live probe.

findings.evidence: Step 2.5 offers `--extra-json '<json>'` while requiring `--catalog-path`. Its surrounding text calls this a test of the chosen pair and knobs, but cli.py rejects the command if that JSON includes `effort`; leaving effort out probes a different invocation from the configured one.
findings.fix: Specify exactly which applicable non-effort knobs go in --extra-json for the catalog-recording probe. Describe that result as review-pair availability without the chosen effort. If the owner needs the selected level verified as well, use the separate --effort probe without --catalog-path, carrying the same applicable knobs and consent.

findings.evidence: “with no catalog file yet: no proposal path leaves the roster alone” stops a first-time setup even when the owner can supply a model. The existing `confirm-catalog-entry` path explicitly initializes a missing catalog without reading or migrating either roster.
findings.fix: When fetching would migrate an out-of-scope roster, prohibit the fetch but allow an owner-confirmed model to initialize the catalog via confirm-catalog-entry; provide the minimal valid entry shape. If the owner chooses only a session-default lane, allow render-toml without --catalog-path when no catalog exists.

findings.evidence: “It keeps every other table, every unknown key and every comment in the file.” On replacement, `toml_splice.set_array` explicitly removes a deleted lane's body and comments; the replacement prompt likewise offers an unqualified comment-preservation promise.
findings.fix: Qualify both the reference and replacement prompt: unrelated tables and their comments are preserved, but comments attached to deleted lanes or removed policy tables may be lost. Offer a copy of the existing config if the owner needs to retain those comments.

findings.evidence: “`render-toml` silently dropped at least one lane entry” does not follow from every `WARNING:` line. The writer also warns for malformed role-order tables and ladder keys naming no lane, even if every lane entry was written.
findings.fix: Report the specific rejected item from stderr and compare both written lane arrays and ladders against the approved input. Distinguish a dropped lane from a dropped order key or omitted policy table; never describe the latter two as deleted lanes.

findings.evidence: “only on a successful write; a failed one keeps it” leaves no cleanup for a canceled wizard after catalog scratch was made. The catalog reference also tells the agent to save optional web results under the project's tmp folder, outside the scratch directory Step 0 says must contain every temporary file.
findings.fix: Put the web-result JSON in the same private scratch directory and define cleanup for cancellation, ordinary early stops and successful completion. Retain scratch only for a diagnosed failure where inspection is useful, and report the retained path.
